subject: Tiered SLO proposal: uptime %, P95 latency slabs, and monthly credit escrow
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novafin.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Megan Liu <megan.liu@novafin.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify SLA matrix for pilot — uptime targets and latency SLOs

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Redwood runtime looked promising. Before we sign the pilot PO we need a clearer SLA template from your side. Two items are priorities for our legal & infra teams:

- A baseline uptime percentage (monthly) and the exact credit calculation if we miss that.
- An explicit latency SLO (P95) for inference responses for our real-time endpoints, and how latency breaches translate to credits.

Also: we operate in banking prod workloads; any maintenance windows and regional failover carveouts must be explicit. Finally, can you confirm whether you will accept a monthly credit cap expressed as a percentage of monthly invoice, or whether you prefer fixed dollar caps?

Looking for something we can attach to the PO this week.

Thanks — Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform, Novafin
[Attachment: Novafin-pilot-requirements.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novafin.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 10:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify SLA matrix for pilot — uptime targets and latency SLOs

Sanjay —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've pulled together a short proposal (attached) that attempts to balance predictability for you with operational guardrails on our side. High level summary below; full draft attached (SLA-draft-v3.pdf).

Key points:
- Uptime: standard baseline of 99.95% monthly for hosted endpoints. Remedy is monthly service credits calculated as % of monthly invoice (see tier table in attachment).
- Latency (P95): we propose a P95 target of 250ms for single-token response time on our standard hosted tier (measured at Redwood edge within region). Breaches are measured per calendar month.
- Credit mapping: small breach windows convert to incremental % credits. For combined availability + latency hits in the same month we apply the higher of the two remedies, capped at a monthly limit.
- Monthly cap options: (A) fixed cap of 25% of monthly invoice, or (B) escrowed credit pool for pilot = 10% pre-funded credit (redeemable against incidents) — we can do either; we'd recommend escrow for a 3-month pilot to accelerate approvals.
- Maintenance carveouts: planned maintenance (48h rolling notice for non-emergency), region failover, and customer-induced misconfig are excluded. Emergency maintenance will be notified and tracked; it consumes the same monthly budget for credits.

Can your legal/infra folks review the attached and tell us if the escrow approach would work for Novafin? If escrow is acceptable we will provide DocuSign + wiring instructions.

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA-draft-v3.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Megan Liu <megan.liu@novafin.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novafin.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed tweaks to credit math and latency measurement

Quick internal note (copied Novafin so we're transparent):

Grace / Laura — a couple suggestions before we lock the draft:

1) Credit cap: recommend making the monthly cap a function of average monthly invoice across prior 3 months for existing customers; for pilots use fixed % of PO (easier). For our pilot ask, keep escrow = 10% of PO and a separate cap of 25% of invoice for extreme cases.

2) Latency measurement: define P95 over request-to-first-byte for full payloads (not single-token) — customers often measure differently. If Novafin wants single-token we should list both (P95 token = 250ms, P95 rtt = 400ms) and make credits tied to the customer-selected metric.

3) Escrow mechanics: propose escrow be refundable if no credit draws in the first 90 days; draws are documented via incident IDs + postmortem.

If Laura signs off I'll update the attached worksheet (monthly-credit-worksheet.xlsx) and circulate final DocuSign link.

Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novafin.com>, Megan Liu <megan.liu@novafin.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Final pilot SLA proposal and next steps (escrow path)

Sanjay / Megan —

Thanks for the quick review. Based on your feedback and Ben's edits, here's what we're putting forward for the pilot PO:

- Baseline uptime: 99.95% monthly (hosted endpoints).
- Latency SLOs (choose measurement method in PO):
  * Option 1 (token-level): P95 single-token generation = 250ms.
  * Option 2 (request-level): P95 end-to-first-byte = 400ms.
- Credit structure: tiered monthly credits tied to severity bands in SLA-draft-v3.pdf. Credits are expressed as percentages of that month's invoice.
- Monthly cap for pilot: escrow model — Novafin pre-funds 10% of pilot PO into a credit escrow. Draws against escrow documented with incident IDs & postmortems; any unused escrow refunded after 90 days. Separate extreme-case cap remains 25% of monthly invoice.
- Maintenance & carveouts: planned maintenance with 48h notice, regional failover, and customer misconfig excluded. Emergency maintenance handled case-by-case but will be captured in incident logs.

Attachments: SLA-draft-v3.pdf (full text of proposed SLA), monthly-credit-worksheet.xlsx (example math). DocuSign link for escrow addendum: https://docusign.net/XXYYZZ12345

Next steps: if this aligns, sign the PO + escrow addendum and we'll provision pilot capacity within 5 business days. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the math.

Regards,
Grace
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: monthly-credit-worksheet.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)]
